predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Vaspurakan, the Artsruni lands round Lake Van, held until 908 under Abbasid suzerainty: Khatchik-Gagik II Artsruni 'was the first of the Artsrunis to rule Vaspurakan under Abbasid suzerainty'

predecessors.name: Bagratid Armenia
predecessors.text: Vaspurakan, inside Cliopatria's Bagratid Armenia shapes of 886-910 until the Artsruni kingdom was recognised in 908

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: the whole kingdom: 'the Kingdom of Vaspurakan became the Byzantine theme of Vasprakania'

ledger.x: 908: Gagik Artsruni is recognised as king and Vaspurakan stands as a kingdom between Lake Van and Lake Urmia.
1021: King Senekerim-Hovhannes gives Vaspurakan to the Byzantine Empire.

wars.name: Artsruni-Sajid alliance against the Bagratid kingdom
wars.outcome: No border result recorded: 'Gagik I Artsruni was recognized as king by the Sajid ruler Yusuf and allied with the latter to attack the Bagratuni kingdom'; after Smbat's death at Yusuf's hands in 914 'Gagik allied with the new Bagratuni king Ashot II'.

wars.name: Seljuk raid on Vaspurakan
wars.outcome: 'In 1016, the kingdom was devastated by a raid by the Seljuq Turks'; no land changed hands, but harassment by the Seljuk Turks is the Basil II page's reason for the 1021 surrender.

certainty.note: A highland kingdom described by lakes and 35 cantons; no treaty or survey line is on any page.
